subject.title: Feature: Agent 动态切换命令（不重启 Gateway）

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic session-level `/agent <id>` switch for channel conversations, and should that reuse the existing `/agents` command family or stay separate from thread-bound agent commands?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent contract affects command semantics, session identity, cross-agent authorization, storage, and channel routing, so automation should not choose the product/security model on its own.

options.title: Add a generic authorized switch
options.body: Define a bounded conversation/session state contract, allowed-target policy, authorized sender checks, and channel-routing integration before implementing `/agent <id>`.

options.title: Keep current surfaces only
options.body: Leave configured-agent switching to TUI, Feishu dynamic-agent creation, static bindings, and `/focus` for bound sessions rather than adding a chat-level route switch.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API design
options.body: Require a plugin/channel API proposal first if maintainers want this to be channel-specific or outside core.

recommendation.title: Add a generic authorized switch
recommendation.body: Define a bounded conversation/session state contract, allowed-target policy, authorized sender checks, and channel-routing integration before implementing `/agent <id>`.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest current-main routing owner signal across the command registry, session protocol, and Feishu dynamic-route surfaces involved in the decision.
